---
title: A small library, thoughtfully built
subtitle: On keeping good ideas close, and giving them room to breathe.
---

Good documentation feels like a well-kept notebook. There is a clear place to
begin, enough space to think, and a useful example just when you need one.
The page makes room for the work.

## Begin with a simple idea

Imagine a little library of things you want to return to: an essay, a useful
function, a question that deserves a second look. Each entry needs a title,
a few words of context, and a way to find it again.

```{.python filename="library.py"}
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Entry:
    title: str
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()

library = [Entry("The art of paying attention", ("reading",))]
```

The code uses **IBM Plex Mono**, with a little more room between lines. Names,
punctuation, and indentation stay distinct. Inline expressions such as
`entry.title` belong comfortably in the surrounding text.

## Leave room for the reader

A useful page has a rhythm: a thought, an example, a pause. Headings mark a
change of subject. A quieter margin keeps the route through the document
visible without competing for attention.[^measure]

> A good notebook is a place to think on paper, and a place to find that
> thought again.

[^measure]: The reading column is capped at 710 pixels, with smaller navigation
    and generous space between the columns.

## A modest set of tools

| Piece | Purpose | Example |
|:------|:--------|:--------|
| A title | Say what the page is about | The reading notebook |
| A tag | Give an idea a second home | `reading`, `python` |
| A link | Connect one thought to another | [Notes](notes/index.qmd) |

This notebook uses the **Nocturne** theme. The sun or moon in the
navigation switches between light and dark. [Make it your own](pages/install.qmd)
with a single theme setting.
